chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Sama'ah, that he was asked about a man who ordered his young slaves to perform Tamattu' Hajj,

He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is upon him to sacrifice on their behalf.' I said, 'Suppose he gave them dirhams, and some of them sacrificed, and some of them kept the dirhams and fasted?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It suffices him from them, and he is at choice; if he wishes, he can leave it (the money with them).' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And if he ordered them and they fasted, it would have sufficed him from them.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a master's sacrificial obligation if his young slaves perform Hajj on his behalf using his money?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the vicarious religious obligations of a master for his young, non-bali slaves during the Hajj of Tamattu'. It establishes that while the master is initially liable for the sacrificial animal (udhiyah), providing funds transfers the agency to the slaves, allowing them to choose between sacrificing or fasting, with either act satisfying the master's obligation.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, (It has been narrated) from Sama’at who asked about a man who ordered his servants that they should be performing Tamatto,

he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is upon him that he should sacrifice on their behalf’. I said, ‘Supposing if he was to give them the Dirhams, and some of them were to sacrifice, and some of them were to withhold the Dirhams and Fast?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It would suffice him from them, and he would be with the choice, if he so desires to, he can leave it (the money in their hands)’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And if he has ordered them, and they Fasted, it would have sufficed him from them’.
en.sarwar: 9. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from Sama‘ah who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who instructed his slaves to perform al- Hajj al-Tamattu‘ (advantageous).

He (the Imam) said, ‘He must offer al-Hady (sacrifice) for them.’ I then said, ‘He gave them dirham. Certain ones among them offered sacrifice and others kept the dirham and fasted.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is sufficient for them and he has the choice; if he wants he can leave them (dirham) alone. If he were to instruct them to fast, it would have been sufficient.’”
